text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 0.44% today, continuing a sharp recovery from last week—the stock is up 11% since November 6th. The gains align with a rebound in refining conditions: refineries are running at 95.2% capacity (near peak utilization), heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year due to winter demand, and US crude is holding steady around $90 a barrel. These tighter supply conditions and strong seasonal demand for heating fuels are creating favorable margins for refiners.

However, the broader oil market picture is turning mixed: Russian crude production has rebounded sharply, pushing global oil supplies back into surplus, which could eventually pressure both crude prices and refining margins. The heating oil rally appears to be a near-term tailwind, but if Russian supply continues recovering and global demand softens, that advantage may fade.
